item.title: Asian Stocks Set for Gains as US Inflation Cools: Markets Wrap
item.description: Asian stocks were poised to extend gains Friday as further evidence of moderating US inflation and a pullback in oil prices reinforced bets that the Federal Reserve will refrain from raising interest rates next month.

item.title: Reddit Shares Surge on S&P 500 Inclusion Later This Month
item.description: Reddit Inc. will join the S&P 500 next week as part of an off-cycle change, S&P Dow Jones Indices said Thursday, sending the social networking platform’s shares surging more than 10% after the bell.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 14
item.description: Oil held a decline as traders monitored efforts toward a deal that could reopen the Strait of Hormuz, while more attacks on tankers and energy infrastructure kept the market on edge.

item.title: SEC Delays Crypto Regulation Meeting in Latest Industry Setback
item.description: The Securities and Exchange Commission canceled a Friday meeting where the agency was expected to unveil new plans for digital assets as landmark crypto legislation remains stalled in Congress.

item.title: Judge Orders Kalshi to Stop Offering Most Wagers in Washington
item.description: Kalshi was told by a judge to stop offering most of its prediction market contracts in Washington state, after regulators said they likely constituted an illegal gambling operation.

item.title: OpenAI’s Revenue Run Rate Tops $40 Billion Ahead of IPO
item.description: OpenAI is on track to generate annualized revenue of more than $40 billion based on its current performance, according to people familiar with the matter, roughly doubling its run rate from the end of 2025 and bolstering the company’s plans for a Wall Street debut.

item.title: Why It’s So Hard to Measure the Economy’s Real Potential
item.description: It’s tough to measure the economy’s true potential

item.title: Winklevosses’ Gemini Posts Another Loss, Revenue Increases
item.description: Gemini Space Station Inc., the digital-asset platform led by the billionaires Tyler and Cameron Winklevoss that went public last year just before the crypto market tumbled from record highs, posted a fourth consecutive quarterly loss since the IPO.

item.title: Apple App Store Commission-Rate Proceedings Can Move Forward
item.description: Apple Inc. must take part in a lower court proceeding over the rate it charges developers for sales outside its App Store after the Supreme Court rejected a bid by the iPhone-maker to pause all further action in the case.

item.title: UAE, Qatari Firms Debut in Venezuela Through BP-Led Gas Deal
item.description: Arab Gulf companies are making their debut in Venezuela through an offshore natural gas project to be operated by BP Plc.

item.title: Applied Materials Forecast Gets Tepid Reaction After Rally
item.description: Applied Materials Inc. delivered an estimate-beating forecast that still got a lukewarm reaction from investors, a sign of the lofty hopes surrounding a company that’s key to the AI boom.

item.title: Tyson to Close More Beef Plants as US Cattle Shortage Drags On
item.description: Tyson Foods Inc. said it would close several additional beef plants, in the latest sign of the US beefpacking industry’s restructuring amid a prolonged US cattle shortage.

item.title: OpenAI, Anthropic Tout New Metric to Better Gauge AI’s Cost
item.description: The AI firms want customers to rethink the price of using their models.

item.title: Diversified Said to Near Deal for Elliott-Backed Birch
item.description: Diversified Energy Co. is in advanced talks to acquire Elliott Investment Management-backed oil and gas company Birch Resources for more than $1.7 billion in cash, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: NYC Pied-a-Terre Tax Can Proceed for Now, Appeals Court Says
item.description: The rollout of New York’s pied-à-terre tax can proceed for now after an appeals court temporarily put a hold on a Staten Island judge’s order blocking the plan.

item.title: Argentina’s Inflation Edged Up Last Month on Winter Holidays
item.description: Argentina’s monthly inflation edged up in July, snapping three months of slower readings, in a slight setback for President Javier Milei.

item.title: Workday Shares Surge After Report Silver Lake Is in Talks to Buy Company
item.description: Workday Inc. shares jumped after a Reuters report that private equity firm Silver Lake is in talks to purchase the software provider.

item.title: Podcast Divorces Are Testing the Loyalties of Diehard Fans
item.description: When wedded co-hosts decide to consciously uncouple, who gets custody of the fans?

item.title: BlackRock’s Rieder Says Yen Rebound Hinges on BOJ Hawkishness
item.description: Supporting the yen will take more than government intervention and will need hawkish signals from the Bank of Japan, said Rick Rieder, chief investment officer for global fixed income at BlackRock Inc.

item.title: Hertz Shares Fall After Ackman’s Pershing Sells Stake in Firm
item.description: Hertz Global Holdings Inc. shares tumbled as Pershing Square Inc.’s chief investment officer said the asset management firm has sold its stake in the car-rental company.

item.title: Jane Street Lease Backs $2.25 Billion of Green Data-Center Bonds
item.description: Zenith Arc, an Oklahoma data center project that is leasing its capacity to Jane Street, is selling $2.25 billion of green bonds, adding to the flurry of builders tapping the market for environmentally focused debt.

item.title: Selena Gomez Accused of Fraud by Mental-Health Startup Investors
item.description: Pop star Selena Gomez is being accused of fraud by investors who claim she failed to deliver on promises to leverage her global celebrity and social-media following to promote her mental-health startup, which collapsed last year.

item.title: Second Supertanker Seen Loading at Saudi Oil Hub in Persian Gulf
item.description: A second supertanker appeared moored at Saudi Arabia’s main oil export terminal inside the Persian Gulf, a further sign that loadings at the hub may be picking up as the kingdom’s alternative shipping route through the Red Sea comes under threat.

item.title: US Robot Vacuum Maker One-Ups China Rivals With Voice Commands
item.description: The device, from Silicon Valley brand Matic, can be controlled fully by voice instructions, helping it stand apart from the competition.

item.title: Google Debuts New Gemini Flash While Top AI Model Still Delayed
item.description: Alphabet Inc.’s Google released another installment of its workhorse Gemini Flash artificial intelligence model, but didn’t say when it would release its most powerful AI model, Gemini 3.5 Pro, which has been hampered by delays.

item.title: Housing Crisis Fuels Surge in Mortgage Muni Bond Securitizations
item.description: The nation’s affordable-housing shortage is fueling a fast-growing corner of the municipal bond market, as lenders securitize portfolios of multifamily mortgages to free up capital for new loans.

item.title: Fintech Chime Explores Stablecoins as New Feature on Its App
item.description: Chime Financial Inc. is exploring how to bring stablecoins into its consumer banking platform, in the latest sign that the new form of money is evolving beyond crypto markets and into everyday payments.

item.title: OpenAI Hires New Chief Revenue Officer After Less Than a Year
item.description: OpenAI is naming its second new chief revenue officer in less than a year, a sign of efforts to bolster sales growth ahead of a highly anticipated Wall Street debut.

item.title: Podcaster Alex Cooper is Shutting Down Unwell Beverages
item.description: The superstar podcaster launched a line of drinks in 2025 in partnership with Nestlé and sold at Target stores

item.title: Goldman $2.25 Billion Neos Deal Raises Stakes in Active-ETF Race
item.description: Goldman Sachs Group Inc.’s agreement to buy Neos Investments for as much as $2.25 billion marks a new front in Wall Street’s ETF battle: paying up for specialist firms that have found growth beyond the industry’s low-fee giants.
